title: Determinants and acyclic trivializations along a two-term filtration
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $N\subseteq L\subseteq P$ be inclusions of two-term cochain complexes of $R$-modules, zero outside degrees $-1,0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $M=L/N$, $Q=P/N$ and $S=P/L$ with quotient differentials, and assume that all terms of $N,L,P,M,Q,S$ are finite projective (direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]). For each such complex $E$ set $D(E)=\det_R(E^0)\otimes_R\det_R(E^{-1})^\vee$, where $\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,R)$ and determinant lines and kernel-first exact-sequence maps are those of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence]. For a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$, define $G_{A,B,C}:D(C)\otimes_R D(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(B)$ by the degree-zero kernel-first determinant map tensored with the inverse dual of the degree-minus-one map, using ordinary tensor symmetry. Write $\Xi=G_{N,L,M}$. Then, for all $x\in D(S)$, $z_M\in D(M)$, and $z_N\in D(N)$,
$$G_{N,P,Q}\bigl(G_{M,Q,S}(x\otimes z_M)\otimes z_N\bigr)=G_{L,P,S}\bigl(x\otimes\Xi(z_M\otimes z_N)\bigr).$$
If $d_N,d_M,d_L$ are isomorphisms, let $\delta_E\in D(E)$ correspond to $\det(d_E)$ under $D(E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(\det_R(E^{-1}),\det_R(E^0))$ for $E=N,M,L$. Then $\Xi(\delta_M\otimes\delta_N)=\delta_L$. Both identities hold for arbitrary local ranks, including rank zero, with precisely the displayed ordinary tensor permutations. In each degree the iterated maps in the first identity agree with the kernel-first map for the filtration $N^i\subseteq L^i\subseteq P^i$: a local basis wedge is sent to the ordered wedge of the $N^i$ basis, lifts of the $M^i$ basis into $L^i$, and lifts of the $S^i$ basis into $P^i$.

source.place: Tag 0FJL (lemma-compose-surjections), omitted proof and its hints; Tags 0FJC (lemma-det-ses-functorial) and 0FJD (lemma-det-filtration).

proof.text: Every degreewise quotient sequence in the statement splits: lift the identity of its projective quotient along the surjection using [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Thus localization preserves these sequences (localize their direct-sum splittings). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] to the finitely many terms and refine to a simultaneous finite free cover by taking products of the cover elements. These products generate the unit ideal, by multiplying expressions for $1$ on the original covers. By [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons], determinants, duals, evaluation, ordinary symmetry and the kernel-first maps commute with these localizations. Consequently so do the explicitly defined $G$ maps and $\delta_E$: for the latter the localized top exterior map of $d_E$ acts on a wedge by applying $d_E$ to every factor. It suffices to prove the identities on these charts and use [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] on their differences. Work on one such chart below.

source.place: Tags 0FJD (lemma-det-filtration), localization hint; 0FJB (lemma-det-ses); scalar comparisons in Section 0FJ9 (section-determinants).

proof.text: In each degree $i=-1,0$, choose ordered bases $n_i,m_i,s_i$ of $N^i,M^i,S^i$, lift $m_i$ to $\widetilde m_i$ in $L^i$ and lift $s_i$ to $\widetilde s_i$ in $P^i$. Exactness shows that $(n_i,\widetilde m_i)$ is a basis of $L^i$ and $(n_i,\widetilde m_i,\widetilde s_i)$ a basis of $P^i$: subtract lifts of the quotient coordinates to express any vector in the kernel; applying the quotient map to a relation first kills its quotient coefficients, then injectivity kills the kernel coefficients. The images $(m_i,\overline{\widetilde s_i})$ form a basis of $Q^i$. The wedge formula of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] sends both parenthesizations of $n_i\otimes m_i\otimes s_i$ to $p_i=n_i\wedge\widetilde m_i\wedge\widetilde s_i$. As this tensor is a basis of the source line, the two degreewise maps agree. This also proves the final ordered-wedge clause.

source.place: Tag 0FJD (lemma-det-filtration), explicit computation in its hint, using Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses).

proof.text: Write $e_E^i$ for the determinant basis just chosen for each module, and put $u_E=e_E^0\otimes(e_E^{-1})^\vee$, where the dual basis takes value $1$ on $e_E^{-1}$. Unwinding the definition of $G$ and the wedge formula of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] gives $G_{A,B,C}(u_C\otimes u_A)=u_B$ for each sequence in the flag: in degree zero it sends the kernel and quotient bases to the concatenated basis; in degree $-1$ the inverse dual sends their dual tensor to the functional taking value $1$ on that same concatenation. Ordinary tensor symmetries introduce no scalar. Both sides of the first asserted identity therefore send $u_S\otimes u_M\otimes u_N$ to $u_P$. All three source lines are free of rank one on this chart, so multilinearity gives the equality for every $x,z_M,z_N$.

source.place: Tags 0FJD (lemma-det-filtration) and 0FJL (lemma-compose-surjections), determinant-line assembly with ordinary tensor permutations.

proof.text: For the acyclic identity, choose bases $n$ of $N^{-1}$ and $m$ of $M^{-1}$ and lifts $\widetilde m$ in $L^{-1}$. Use $d_N n$ as basis of $N^0$ and $d_M m$ as basis of $M^0$, possible because these differentials are isomorphisms. The vectors $d_L\widetilde m$ lift $d_M m$ by the chain equation. Hence $(n,\widetilde m)$ and $(d_N n,d_L\widetilde m)$ are bases of $L^{-1}$ and $L^0$, by the kernel/quotient coordinate argument of Step 2. Let $n_\wedge,m_\wedge,\ell_\wedge$ denote their degree-minus-one wedges, with $\ell_\wedge=n\wedge\widetilde m$. By definition $\delta_N=(\bigwedge d_N)(n_\wedge)\otimes n_\wedge^\vee$ and likewise for $M,L$. The degree-zero kernel-first map of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] sends $(\bigwedge d_N)(n_\wedge)\otimes(\bigwedge d_M)(m_\wedge)$ to $(\bigwedge d_L)(\ell_\wedge)$, and its degree-minus-one inverse dual sends $n_\wedge^\vee\otimes m_\wedge^\vee$ to $\ell_\wedge^\vee$. Thus the defining ordinary permutation in $\Xi$ gives exactly $\Xi(\delta_M\otimes\delta_N)=\delta_L$.

source.place: Tag 0FJC (lemma-det-ses-functorial), differential diagram; compare lemma-canonical-element-well-defined in Section 0FJI.

proof.text: For any fixed input the difference of the two global expressions maps to zero on every member of Step 1's unit-ideal cover, so [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] makes it zero. Apply this both to the trilinear identity and to the differential elements. The local computations used empty wedges equal to $1$, with their dual functional also equal to $1$, so include every zero-rank case without a permutation sign. Ranks may differ between charts because the argument is chartwise. If $R$ is the zero ring all modules and maps have one underlying element, and the same identities hold.
